description: The iteration. A trigger becomes a measured brief; the Steward proposes the next increment as a choice, an interview or a request for the goal; the person answers in the application; the answer becomes a spec brief; the Steward writes a change spec inside a closed grammar; the policy gate approves, asks the person or refuses; an approved spec is applied by the headless coder in the pack repository, verified, installed and released as a new pack version; the brain observes and the next iteration starts. Every path ends in a place the person reads.

places.p-steward-prompts: The Steward's questions: choices, interviews, goal requests, approvals
places.p-steward-specs: Change specs (draft, approved, rejected, refused, applied, released, rolled-back)
places.p-steward-refused: Specs the gate refused, with the reason
places.p-steward-decisions: The person's and the gate's decisions (spec approval, rejection, rollback)
places.p-steward-runs: Runs: branch, pack version, coder summary, verification, release
places.p-steward-build-log: Apply, verify and release command results

transitions.label: Render a brief
transitions.description: steward-context renders the charter, the latest health, the lanes, the model map, the knowledge, the plan and the history into one brief token; for a spec brief it adds the person's answer.

transitions.label: Propose the next increment (choice, interview or goal)

agent.nl:
You are the Steward, a persona whose job is the model it lives in, deciding with the person what the next increment is. Read the brief, then reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else.

${ctx.data.brief}

Choose the mode:
- "goal" when the brief says the goal is NOT DEFINED: ask the person what this model should become; give 3 example goal statements they can adapt (a developer persona for one kind of service, a research desk, a cheaper and more deterministic version of the nets already there); the question asks for the goal in one line plus a paragraph.
- "interview" when the next increment cannot be chosen without information only the person has (which nets matter, what a lane may cost, who consumes an output): ask at most 3 precise questions; each question is an option {value: "q1", label: <the question>, description: <why the answer matters>}.
- "choice" otherwise: propose 3 or 4 concrete next increments, each one change spec of one kind from the closed grammar: tune, view, crystallise, add-lane, remove-lane, add-net, add-script, app. Prefer, in this order: a lane with errors or contract misses, stranded tokens, a lane that costs more than its siblings, a big net without views, an agent lane whose fires look identical (crystallise), then the goal's most valuable missing capability. Never propose anything that touches the protected set named in the brief. If the brief carries THE PLAN, the options are its next planned increments in order; deviate only with a stated reason. Each option: {value: "opt-1", label: <one line>, description: <what and why, two sentences>, kind: <spec kind>, nets: [<net ids touched>], effort: "S|M|L", risk: "low|medium|high", evidence: [<signal lines from the brief>], recommended: true|false}. Exactly one option is recommended.

Reply with exactly this shape: {"promptId": "<promptId from the brief>", "iterationId": "<iterationId from the brief>", "mode": "choice|interview|goal", "question": "<the question to the person, one sentence>", "context": "<two sentences: what the last observation showed, what changed last time>", "options": [...], "allowFreeText": true, "rationale": "<why these options, two sentences>", "at": "<now from the brief>"}

transitions.label: Reshaped question to a new proposal brief
Policy gate: approve, ask the person, or refuse
transitions.description: steward-gate checks the spec against the charter: closed kinds, the protected set, the scope, the budget, the autonomy level. It writes an approval decision, a question for the person, or a refusal with the reason.

transitions.label: Apply: the coder edits the pack on a branch, build, package
transitions.description: steward-apply spawns the configured headless agent (p-steward-coders, chosen by the charter) inside the pack repository with the spec, the charter, the compact-source conventions, the knowledge and the protected set as its brief; then inlines the library, builds and packages the pack, bumps the version, checks the invariants and queues verification.

transitions.label: Verify: invariants, lint, publish, install, smoke, or roll back
Release: merge, tag, record, observe, next iteration; or roll back
